paragraphs.source_en: The three major styles, namely the Bubaline, Round Heads and Pastoral styles, may have been contemporaneous in certain periods. The Bubaline style and the Round Heads may have coexisted in the Early Holocene until the Neolithic period, each present in the different geographical region. The Pastoral style coexisted with the two previous styles in the Neolithic period in the regions with both Bubaline engravings and the Round Head paintings.

units.source_en: The three major styles, namely the Bubaline, Round Heads and Pastoral styles, may have been contemporaneous in certain periods.
The Bubaline style and the Round Heads may have coexisted in the Early Holocene until the Neolithic period, each present in the different geographical region.
The Pastoral style coexisted with the two previous styles in the Neolithic period in the regions with both Bubaline engravings and the Round Head paintings.

paragraphs.source_en: The Pastoral style cannot be dated earlier than at 7,500 BP when the domesticated animals are archaeologically attested to in the Central Sahara, although some authors believe they have found earlier pastoral engravings dating to before 7,840+330 BP (Striedter et al. 2002-3). Regarding the presence of domesticated cattle among the Bubaline engravings, the following explanation is possible; the Bubaline style originated as early as 10,000 BP or earlier, representing exclusively wild animals. With the introduction of domesticated cattle at around 7,500 BP the logical consequence was the representation of these animals, since they took the dominant place in the economy and ideology, previously occupied only by wild animals.

paragraphs.source_en: The difference in age, over several millennia, between various engravings cannot be evidenced by the desert varnish because it formed mainly between 6,100 and 5,100 BP (Cremaschi 1996; Mori 2000), meaning that it covered all engravings made in various periods with the same dark patina. The Bubaline and the Pastoral engravings made in the same places may thus represent a several millennia long artistic activity.
